landscape.label: Why Window Film Here
landscape.title: Why Window Film Makes Sense in New York City Buildings
landscape.say: Most New Yorkers cannot replace their windows. In a co-op or condo the windows often belong to the building, replacement needs board approval and an architect, and in a landmarked building the Landmarks Preservation Commission may have a say about anything that changes the facade. Window film goes on the inside face of the glass you already have.

landscape.say: For homes: Decorative: Etched, patterned and textured films for brownstone doors, transoms, interior glass partitions and bathroom windows. Security: Thick safety film that holds shattered glass together and slows a break-in on garden apartments, ground-floor windows and townhouse doors across the city. Glare Reduction: Reduce screen glare and squinting from river views, open sky and sunlight reflected off the glass building across the street, without making rooms gloomy. Energy-Saving: Cuts the solar gain that drives summer cooling, and low-E versions also hold heat indoors in January, so apartments and houses depend less on the AC and the radiators.

landscape.say: For businesses: Solar Control: Solar control film for commercial buildings with large glass exposures, reducing cooling load and hot zones near the curtain wall in summer. Conference Room Privacy: Frosted and patterned film for glass-walled conference rooms and offices, giving teams visual privacy without losing the open look of the floor. Low-E: Low-emissivity film that reflects room heat back inside in winter and rejects solar heat in summer, a lower-cost glazing upgrade for older NYC buildings. Office: Glare control, heat rejection and privacy for Manhattan, Brooklyn and Queens offices, installed after hours to work around tenants and building rules.

landscape.label: Local Know-How
landscape.title: Prewar Co-ops, Brownstones and Glass Condo Towers
landscape.say: The housing stock here ranges from 1900s walk-ups with wood double-hung sashes to 2010s condo towers with floor-to-ceiling insulated glass. Those are very different jobs. Old single-pane sashes accept almost any film, while large insulated units in newer towers need a film matched to the glass so the inner pane does not absorb too much heat and stress the seal or the glass edge.

landscape.label: How It Works
landscape.title: How an install works

tiles.s: Start with the online form: give them the address
They confirm whether the glass is single-pane
Many NYC buildings want a certificate of insurance

landscape.say: Here's how an install works. First, start with the online form: give them the address, the floor, the direction the windows face and the problem you want gone. Then, they confirm whether the glass is single-pane, insulated or laminated, look at frame condition and show film samples on your actual windows. On install day, many NYC buildings want a certificate of insurance, a scope of work and a booked service elevator before any contractor arrives. Finally, installers protect sills and floors, clean each pane, apply the film and squeegee it out.
